transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-25
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Thompson (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Aurora CTO), Leah Wong (Aurora Lead Eng), Carlos Reyes (Aurora DevOps), Nina Gomez (Aurora PM)

Summary: Quick integration walkthrough of Redwood SDKs (Python + TypeScript), auth and env setup, and high-level POC plan.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we can do intros real quick, i'm jordan from redwood, maya will run through code and i'll cover procurement/next steps
[00:20] Samir: yeah thanks jordan, i'm samir, cto at aurora tech, we have leah and carlos here to dig into the SDKs. nina is on for timeline and success criteria
[00:35] Maya: cool, i'll jump into the screen share in a second, first quick context: you mentioned wanting embedding search and a chat assistant for ops runbooks, is that right?
[00:50] Samir: correct, primary use is internal knowledge and triage, latency matters but cost is also a factor, likely start hosted then move to dedicated or private for compliance
[01:10] Leah: and we need SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration because of PII in some runbooks
[01:22] Maya: got it, we'll cover auth patterns and how those map to hosted vs private in a moment. I'll open the quickstart repo - note, the repo link is in chat: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts (shared)
[01:45] Maya: starting with python, pip install is straightforward. Example: pip install redwood-sdk-cli (note: transcript may mis-hear package name, actual repo has redwood-sdk and redwood-client, i'll send exact link)
[02:05] [crosstalk] Carlos: sorry did you say redwood-sdk-cli?
[02:08] Maya: yeah i said it loosely, the package name in pip is redwood-client, apologies for the slip, we'll include exact commands in the quickstart readme
[02:20] Maya: code snippet readout: from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) - simple env var pattern
[02:39] Leah: how do we do rotation of keys and secrets at scale? we use vault and cloud kms
[02:46] Maya: you can store REDWOOD_API_KEY in vault and inject into CI/CD or runtime. For Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations for key wrapping, and we export audit logs to your SIEM
[03:05] Jordan: just to add, for hosted API we do offer short-lived key patterns and recommend rotation every 30 days for service accounts, we'll send the security whitepaper after the call
[03:20] [00:03:20] Samir: ok good, also curious about typescript - node support and streaming?
[03:30] Maya: yes, typescript/npm: npm i @redwood-inference/sdk and import { Redwood } from '@redwood-inference/sdk'; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); and we support streaming responses via events or async iterators, there's an examples/streaming.ts in the quickstart repo
[03:55] Maya: note, small transcripts errors - package names in the demo window looked slightly different because i had a local alias, i'll push the exact package names in chat and the repo
[04:10] [00:04:10] Carlos: what about local dev env - are there docker images or local mocks?
[04:20] Maya: yep we provide a local mock server in the repo for quick dev feedback, plus a docker compose example that emulates batching behavior. For heavier load tests we provide a load harness spreadsheet and a k6 script in benchmarks/
[04:40] Leah: nice, and for auth we want to use SSO. how does SSO map to API keys for engineers vs service accounts?
[04:52] Maya: good question. SSO/SSO with SAML/SCIM handles user login to the console, then service accounts can be created with limited scopes that generate API keys. Admins manage RBAC in the console, and keys can be scoped to routes/models and have expiry
[05:12] Jordan: on the enterprise plan, you also get tenant-level audit trails and per-route auth. we'll include screenshots of RBAC controls in the admin console doc
[05:30] [00:05:30] Samir: about environment setup — we run in multiple regions, any caveats?
[05:40] Maya: for hosted, choose region closest to your users to reduce latency; for Dedicated we can colocate pools in your cloud region or on-prem racks. For private deployments, networking is customer-managed and we have a control plane handshake for upgrades
[06:00] Maya: quick demo: i'll show a python quickstart. (screen) repo/quickstarts/python/README — step 1: export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<your-key>"; step 2: python run_chat.py --model=redwood-versa-1 --prompt="status page"
[06:28] [00:06:28] Maya: run_chat.py uses client.stream_responses(prompt) and prints tokens as they arrive; this mimics streaming via SSE or websockets depending on the SDK consumer
[06:45] Leah: can we pin model versions? we need deterministic behavior for audits
[06:50] Maya: yes, you can pin to model versions, and we support model rollouts/canary via the console with traffic split rules and automatic fallback on errors
[07:06] [00:07:06] Samir: how about quantization and cost control? we need to keep token costs low for high-volume internal queries
[07:18] Maya: Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles and batching settings by workload. In Dedicated you can choose quantized model variants that reduce memory and cost; we'll show recommend profiles after we see sample traffic
[07:35] Jordan: and for the POC we can run a short benchmark to produce an expected cost per 1M tokens estimate
[07:46] [00:07:46] Carlos: networking questions - for private deployment, does redwood need inbound access? our infra forbids inbound from public internet
[07:58] Maya: for on-prem private deployments we support air-gapped packaging; for VPC mode we set up VPC peering or private link depending on cloud provider. We'll work with your network team on the exact topology
[08:18] Maya: note: occasionally network terms got mangled in my demo - the repo has diagrams under docs/networking.png which i'll attach
[08:30] [00:08:30] Samir: any limitations on concurrency or seq length?
[08:40] Maya: limits depend on your Dedicated pool size; hosted tiers have documented per-second qps and token rate limits. Sequence lengths above 4k tokens invoke different execution kernels and may change throughput; we can profile with your corpus
[09:02] [00:09:02] Maya: switching to typescript quickstart - examples/ts/quickstart.ts. Example usage: const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-versa-1', input: 'foo' }); console.log(resp.output_text)
[09:22] Maya: for streaming in ts we show both EventSource and web socket hooks; the SDK exposes onToken callbacks for client-side rendering
[09:35] Leah: any docs about cost attribution at token-level? we need to billback to teams
[09:44] Jordan: console provides token-level cost and latency dashboards by route and model, and you can tag requests with tenant or team ids to split costs. We'll share a screenshot in the follow-up
[09:58] [00:09:58] Samir: security: where do logs live and for how long? retention policies?
[10:08] Maya: default retention is 90 days for hosted logs, extended retention available as add-on. For Dedicated/Private you control retention and log export to your SIEM. We redact by default sensitive fields, and show configurable PII redaction rules
[10:26] Carlos: do you support bringing your own encryption keys (BYOK)?
[10:30] Maya: yes for Dedicated/Private, BYOK via KMS/HSM is supported; we'll include a guide in the shared security pack
[10:40] [00:10:40] Maya: minor transcript note: some acronyms may sound like 'VPC-C' in audio, it's VPC peering or PrivateLink, apologies if it's fuzzy
[10:55] [00:10:55] Maya: i'll demo a short end-to-end, creating a service account in the console, generating API key, and using it in the python quickstart
[11:20] Maya: (clicking) console -> security -> service accounts -> create -> scope = embeddings:write, models:infer -> generate key -> copy
[11:36] [00:11:36] Maya: back in python: export REDWOOD_API_KEY='sk-live-xxxxx' then python examples/embeddings.py --file sample_docs.json -> this writes vector ids to your db (example code shows storing to postgres)
[11:57] Leah: for embeddings, do you provide incremental upserts and similarity search helpers?
[12:05] Maya: yes we have helpers to compute embeddings and batch upserts; the repo includes a basic vector-store adapter for Postgres, Faiss, and Pinecone (we mis-remembered one vendor name in demo earlier, will clarify in notes)
[12:25] [00:12:25] Samir: excellent. timeline: we want a 2-week POC focusing on internal search and chat. is that reasonable?
[12:36] Jordan: yes typical POC is 2-4 weeks. we'll scope success criteria: latency < 300ms for chat 95th pct, and embedding recall > 0.7 on your eval set. We'll draft a POC SOW after we confirm traffic patterns
[12:55] [00:12:55] Nina: can you send a template SOW and a list of required infra access?
[13:05] Jordan: yes, i'll send SOW template and infra checklist. also pricing: we'll send an estimate for hosted vs dedicated for your baseline throughput
[13:24] [00:13:24] Maya: quick note on socket vs http streaming: socket has lower overhead for high concurrency but requires additional infra in browsers; http streaming via fetch is simplest for server-side apps
[13:40] [00:13:40] Carlos: do you support serverless cold-start semantics while keeping the KV cache warm?
[13:51] Maya: we have caching layers and warmers; dedicated pools can keep warm replicas, and the runtime supports KV cache sharing across requests to reduce cold-start token costs
[14:05] [00:14:05] Samir: any gotchas with multi-region data residency?
[14:14] Maya: for hosted we offer EU and US regions; for strict residency we recommend Private deployment in the customer's region or on-prem to ensure data never leaves country borders
[14:30] [00:14:30] Maya: i'll mark this as an action to send region-specific compliance docs and a SOC2 summary
[14:38] [00:14:38] Jordan: can we talk about observability? what traces are available?
[14:45] Maya: per-request tracing, model latency breakdown, token-level timing, and error traces are in the console; we also expose OpenTelemetry hooks to push traces to your APM
[15:00] [00:15:00] Maya: small demo of typescript streaming - (screen) quickstart/ts/streaming.ts showing onToken callback and UI stitching
[15:20] [00:15:20] Leah: nice, that helps. about fallback policies - if a model variant is overloaded do you do automatic downgrade?
[15:30] Maya: yes routing policy can fall back to cheaper/quantized variants automatically; we can define per-route policies and a global fallback tier
[15:42] Jordan: this is useful for predictability in cost spikes during incidents
[15:50] [00:15:50] Samir: ok getting close to time - recap and next steps?
[15:58] Jordan: recap — Maya will share quickstart repo and exact pip/npm package names, security pack and SOC2 summary, and a basic SOW template; we'll aim to schedule POC kickoff for week of 2026-06-08. Aurora to confirm POC success criteria and stakeholders
[16:20] [00:16:20] Maya: action items repeated in chat. i'll also attach docker compose example and k6 scripts for benchmarking
[16:34] Samir: sounds good, appreciate the demo. any quick question on pricing tiers now?
[16:40] Jordan: i'll include a hosted baseline and a dedicated estimate; pricing depends on reserved capacity and instance types for dedicated - we'll propose two sizing options in the estimate
[16:58] [00:16:58] Nina: thanks all, we'll review and circle back by Friday with internal yes/no for kickoff
[17:06] Jordan: perfect, thanks everyone
[17:10] [crosstalk, meeting winds down]
